prompt:
Create ONE finished native editable SVG: FOUR TRUE DIAGONAL VIEWS of the SAME Cinder acolyte for Emberwake, original dark-fantasy action RPG. This is a focused correction of a prior directional pilot: the old pair of front views was nearly identical, the old pair of rear views was nearly identical, and the silhouette was only 20px wide at 32px height. Repair actual 3D turning, depth and scale. Do not repeat those failures. Work like a sculptural fantasy character artist; connected anatomy, cloth weight and three broad value groups. Native vector paths, not a raster wrapped in SVG.

REFERENCE DESIGN, preserve across every view: dusty wine/salmon hooded adult, recessed ash-gray face; angular overlapping shoulder mantle in wine, narrow ivory stitch strip on anatomical LEFT shoulder; robe compressed by plain dark waist belt, uneven split zigzag hem, two soot-dark planted boots. Anatomical RIGHT hand grips a bent dark wooden crook staff with ONE ivory collar; anatomical LEFT hand cups ONE small ochre ember near the ribs. One sleeve hangs longer; other is close fitting. Hood and mantle connect into the shoulders. No armor or jewelry. Palette matches source exactly: wine #753f49, dusty salmon #b3726b, lit cloth #d99886, shadow #432d39, ash face #a6a09a, staff #604b3f, ivory #e5d5af, ember #efb56c. This is text reference continuity, NOT an image edit; redraw the quarters while retaining the individual. No additional characters or hounds.

SHEET: exact SVG viewBox="0 0 1536 768", width1536 height768. TWO columns, TWO rows, each sheet cell768x384. Each cell contains one square384x384 figure workspace centered horizontally: local workspace origins (192,0), (960,0), (192,384), (960,384). Four top-level groups ONLY, id="cultist-se" transform="translate(192 0)", id="cultist-sw" transform="translate(960 0)", id="cultist-ne" transform="translate(192 384)", id="cultist-nw" transform="translate(960 384)". All paths inside each group use LOCAL 0..384 coordinates. Keep each figure within x=35..345,y=22..355. All unused space TRANSPARENT. No background rectangles, labels, arrows, frames, floor, terrain, diamond base, cast/contact shadows, halo, spell trail or spark effects. No visible text, numbers, logo, scripts, external resources, image/use elements, embedded raster, paint-resource IDs or gradients. Explicit colors and simple filled paths; group IDs are for extraction only.

SCALE: all four figures have consistent actual height320-330px and visible width270-300px INCLUDING staff. At0.1 scale each occupies approximately27-30x32-33px. Do not solve detail by making taller figures. The older narrow20px silhouette must become a broader purposeful elbow/mantle/stance contour; do not horizontally stretch the whole body. Same head size, robe length, equipment and anatomy across all four. Two boots contact one virtual ground plane, foreshortened correctly. No bob or running action. Still alert pose, knees soft, weight slightly forward. Common fixed mild elevated ORTHOGRAPHIC camera looks down27degrees, square screen-aligned tactical view, NO diamond-isometric floor. Common light from upper LEFT of the SCREEN in all four cells; screen-right faces dark even when heading reverses. Painted/cut-paper fantasy sculpture with organic curved transitions, not geometric sausages, glossy plastic, flat front/back paper dolls or photoreal PBR.

TURNAROUND REQUIREMENT: SE and SW are opposing FRONT quarters; NE and NW are opposing REAR quarters. Physically rotate one character about its vertical axis while keeping the camera fixed. Shoulder line, belt ellipse, hood opening, robe side overlap, foot direction and anatomical gear must all rotate together. Each view must show one shoulder nearer, the other compressed behind, with a torso SIDE plane visible. Do not merely shift a face inside the same frontal robe. No exact or near-duplicate body outlines. No group mirroring: rebuild overlaps, visibility and light planes. Keep right-hand staff, left-hand ember and left-shoulder stitch panel attached to their anatomical sides; hide them honestly when the torso occludes them. Show the staff going behind or in front of sleeves where appropriate, never through the robe. The four figures must remain recognizably the same garment and person.

SE / TOP LEFT: front-quarter facing lower RIGHT. Hood opening and nose plane point right; viewer sees broad front cloth and a narrower right-facing torso-side plane. Near shoulder projects forward/down; far shoulder recedes. Right hand and bent staff are readable beside one side; left hand cups ember by ribs. One boot projects distinctly toward lower-right, the far boot sits higher behind. The belt and hem cut visibly turn diagonally.

SW / TOP RIGHT: front-quarter facing lower LEFT, a real opposite yaw from SE. Nose/hood opening point left, front-versus-side planes exchange widths. Opposite shoulder now projects, with a visibly DIFFERENT sleeve overlap and elbow negative space. Foremost boot points lower-left, far boot higher behind. Staff remains in anatomical right hand but its grip/shaft occlusion changes; same crook/collar, not a substituted weapon. Ivory left-shoulder stitches remain on anatomical left. Redraw the light from screen upper-left, do not mirror colors. SE and SW must be obviously different silhouettes even at32px.

NE / BOTTOM LEFT: rear-quarter facing upper RIGHT. Large hood BACK, mantle back and rightward torso-side depth dominate; absolutely no ash face on the back. Hood seam and neck overlap angle right, one shoulder recedes. Near boot/heel is broad and lower, far boot/toe points upper-right and is foreshortened. Belt and robe wrap away from viewer, no front opening painted on back. Right hand staff stays attached around the body's turn. Left-hand ember is partly or wholly occluded by torso; a small edge glimpse is enough, never paint it through back cloth.

NW / BOTTOM RIGHT: rear-quarter facing upper LEFT. True opposite rear yaw with leftward hood/spine/hip turn, opposite shoulder depth, distinct robe side overlap and boot direction. NOT a copy of NE. Keep right-hand staff and left-shoulder stitches physically consistent, reveal only surfaces facing camera. Again no front face through hood, no front robe seam on the back. Same upper-left screen light.

Judge the four-turn anatomy and 32px silhouette before details. Use strong asymmetric broad cloth planes, fitted elbows/wrists, recessed face and hood rim in front views, quiet back cloth in rear views. Four useful quarter views are the deliverable, not four icons differing only in face marks or small accents.
